title: Accounts Payable Coordinator
description:
As an Accounts Payable Coordinator in a research-led organisation, based in Oxfordshire, you'll manage supplier invoices, payments, and queries to ensure smooth day-to-day operations. Your role will help keep financial processes accurate and efficient, supporting the wider accounting and finance team.

Client Details

A company in the innovative technology sector located in Oxfordshire.

Description
- Process supplier invoices and ensure timely payments.
- Handle supplier queries and resolve discrepancies efficiently.
- Maintain accurate records of accounts payable transactions.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve outstanding issues.
- Support month-end close processes by providing necessary documentation.
- Assist with audits by preparing and organising relevant financial data.
- Ensure compliance with company policies and financial regulations.
- Collaborate with other departments for smooth financial operations.

Profile

A successful Accounts Payable Coordinator should have:
- Experience working with accounting and finance systems.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Ability to handle supplier queries and resolve issues effectively.
- Familiarity with accounts payable processes and reconciliations.
- Knowledge of financial regulations and compliance requirements.
- Good communication and teamwork skills.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from £28,000 to £35,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Competitive benefits package.
- Flexible working options.
- Supportive team culture.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Paralegal - Commercial & Residential Property
description:
Property Paralegal Oxfordshire

Salary: £28,000 - £30,000

Location: Oxford

Looking for an opportunity where you can develop your experience, work on quality matters and learn from experienced lawyers?

A highly regarded law firm in Oxfordshire is looking to strengthen its Property team with the addition of a Property Paralegal.

This is a great opportunity to join an established team advising a varied client base, including individuals, business owners, entrepreneurs and high-net-worth clients. The firm takes a personal, relationship-led approach, with a focus on delivering quality work rather than operating in a high-volume environment.

The role

You'll work closely with experienced Property lawyers, supporting a varied caseload of residential and commercial property matters. The role offers exposure to bespoke transactions and the opportunity to build your technical knowledge while taking an active role in the progression of matters.

Your work will include:
- Supporting residential and commercial property transactions.
- Assisting with acquisitions, disposals and property investment matters.
- Working on landlord and tenant matters, including leases and lease extensions.
- Drafting legal documents and correspondence.
- Liaising with clients, solicitors and other third parties.
- Undertaking legal research and assisting with more complex matters.
- Supporting the wider team with transaction progression and file management.

What they're looking for

The firm is open to hearing from Property Paralegals, Legal Assistants and experienced Conveyancing professionals looking for a new challenge.

You'll ideally have some previous property experience, a strong eye for detail and a genuine interest in developing your career within the sector. Just as importantly, you'll be organised, client-focused and keen to learn within a close-knit team.

Why consider it?
- Quality over quantity: Work on bespoke matters rather than a high-volume, repetitive caseload.
- Varied exposure: Develop experience across residential and commercial property work.
- Experienced colleagues: Learn directly from established Property lawyers.
- Interesting clients: Support matters for individuals, business owners and HNW clients.
- Career development: Build a strong foundation for your longer-term career in Property.

If you're looking for a role where you can broaden your experience and develop within a quality-focused team, I'd be happy to have a confidential conversation.

Get in touch to find out more.

title: Service Advisor
description:
Service Advisor - Oxford

Location: Oxford

Salary: £30,000 - £38,000 OTE

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

About the Role

We are looking for a professional and customer-focused Service Advisor to join a busy and successful aftersales team in Oxford. Acting as the key link between customers and the workshop, you will ensure every customer receives exceptional service while supporting the efficient operation of the service department.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Service Advisor or a customer service professional with automotive experience who is looking to develop their career within a reputable dealership environment.

Key Responsibilities
- Greet customers and manage service and repair bookings.
- Accurately record customer concerns and vehicle requirements.
- Liaise with workshop technicians regarding vehicle progress and additional work requirements.
- Provide customers with updates throughout the repair process.
- Prepare and explain service invoices and associated costs.
- Promote and sell additional aftersales products and services where appropriate.
- Ensure all administrative tasks are completed accurately and on time.
- Maintain high levels of customer satisfaction and retention.
- Handle customer queries and complaints professionally and effectively.
- Work closely with colleagues across the service and parts departments.

Requirements
- Previous experience as a Service Advisor, Customer Service Advisor, or similar customer-facing role within the automotive industry.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent organisational and administrative abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience using dealership management systems is advantageous.
- Strong attention to detail and customer-focused approach.
- Full UK driving licence preferred.

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary package with realistic OTE of £30,000 - £38,000.
- Manufacturer and in-house training.
- Career development opportunities.
- Pension scheme.
- Employee discounts and benefits package.
- Supportive and professional team environment.
- Modern dealership facilities.

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be passionate about customer service, highly organised, and capable of building strong relationships with customers and colleagues alike. You will take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience while helping the aftersales department achieve its performance objectives.

Salary: £30,000 - £38,000 OTE

Location: Oxford

Position: Full-Time, Permanent

Industry: Automotive Aftersales / Service Department

title: Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator
company: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: PREVIOUS APPLICANTS NEED NOT APPLY Advert - Band 3 Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator - Urology We have some exciting opportunities available to join the Urology team as a Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator. We have a variety of posts based at either the Churchill Hospital (Headington) or the Horton Hospital (Banbury). As a Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator, you will work closely with our clinical teams to support the delivery of excellent care to our patients. Your day-to-day role will involve talking with patients and the clinical teams, carrying out a variety of administrative tasks such as booking clinic appointments, scheduling patients into an operating theatre list, and making sure our consultant and nursing teams' clinic letters are processed and sent out to our patients. These roles are ideal for anyone looking to move into the NHS, with good opportunities for career progression both within and outside the department. We welcome applications from recent school leavers or graduates, or those looking for a change, as full training will be given once you start in your role. Informal discussions or visits to the department are welcomed, please do contact either Lisha Collier or Sandra Hardy (Urology Pathway Managers) for further information. Lisha.Collier@ouh.nhs.uk Sandra.Hardy@ouh.nhs.uk 1. Book new and follow-up outpatient and diagnostic appointments, ensuring that capacity is proactively and efficiently used. This includes booking patients into the correct clinic to ensure that they are seen by the most appropriate clinician. 2. Reschedule outpatient appointments as a result of patients calling the service, in line with local targets and agreed local processes in respect to patient cancellations. 3. Actively review patient DNAs, liaising with the appropriate clinical staff and reschedule patient appointments in line with agreed local processes. 4. Taking telephone calls from patients and actioning their queries or directing them to the appropriate person. 5. Contributing to the management of the daily emails accounts within the department, ensuring that queries are dealt with effectively and efficiently. 6. Completing clinical letters for patients and GPs 7. Adding additional clinic capacity on EPR as directed by management. 8. Liaise with the appropriate teams (e.g. learning disabilities team, translator services etc) to ensure that patients requiring additional support services are not indirectly discriminated. The post holder will be expected to provide day to day administrative support for Urology clinicians within the Urology department. The individual will need to be flexible to meet the competing and evolving demands of the service. There will be an element of cross cover required within the team and an extension of the role to provide administrative support to other services covered by the Urology Team Patient administration underpins the patient journey and supports clinical teams in delivering high quality patient care and can make a real difference to the patient experience. Effective and efficient patient administration supports management through ensuring a high standard of data quality and by making the best use of capacity and resources. The post holder has responsibility for the provision of a professional, comprehensive, and efficient administrative support service for the Urology clinical team
